candidates.name: wppconnect-server
candidates.sessionPersistence: token/session files per instance; multi-session REST
candidates.reconnect: session restore via stored tokens; requires persistent Node process
candidates.securityNotes: REST API must be firewalled; secret keys for API auth; WhatsApp Web unofficial surface
candidates.footprint: heavy (Express server, Socket.IO, full REST stack)
candidates.verdict: viable but heavier than needed for single-controller engineering bridge

candidates.name: whatsapp-web.js
candidates.sessionPersistence: LocalAuth / RemoteAuth session dirs; documented reconnect
candidates.reconnect: reload session from disk on process restart when LocalAuth used
candidates.securityNotes: Puppeteer/Chromium; session dir is secret-equivalent; unofficial WhatsApp Web; BSUID/username protocol changes tracked in open issues
candidates.footprint: light adapter (library + optional Chromium); fits tiny NAC comms module
candidates.verdict: recommended for NAC engineering control bridge proof

recommended.name: whatsapp-web.js
recommended.whyOverAlternatives: Single-controller bridge needs one session, allowlist gate, and GitHub adapter — not a multi-tenant REST server. whatsapp-web.js keeps footprint minimal while matching send/receive/media/session needs. wppconnect-server remains valid if NAC later needs multi-session REST + built-in webhooks without custom adapter code.
